title: Jehovah, Hallelujah
origin: Slave Songs of the United States (1867), No. 2, page 2; from the Port Royal Islands, South Carolina.
note: Source: Slave Songs of the United States (1867), No. 2. Independent PD confirmation: Yale University's Gullah Geechee Spirituals Project, which reproduces the 1867 text.

title: Bound to Go (I Can't Stay Behind)
origin: Slave Songs of the United States (1867); a Sea Islands 'shout' spiritual (No. 5).
note: Source: Slave Songs of the United States (1867), 'Bound to Go.' Independent PD confirmation: PD Info's public-domain music reference, which lists the entire 1867 collection as public domain.
verses:
I can't stay behind, my Lord,
I can't stay behind!
There's room enough, room enough,
Room enough in the heaven, my Lord,
I can't stay behind.

I've been all around, I've been all around,
Been all around the heaven, my Lord;
There's room enough, room enough,
Room enough in the heaven, my Lord,
I can't stay behind.

title: Wrestle On, Jacob
origin: Slave Songs of the United States (1867), No. 6; noted by the editors as probably originating in Virginia.
note: Source: Slave Songs of the United States (1867), No. 6. Independent PD confirmation: the Traditional Ballad Index, which documents its 1867 collection origin.
verses:
O wrestle on, Jacob,
Jacob, day is a-breaking;
Wrestle on, Jacob,
O he would not let him go!

I hold my brother with a trembling hand,
The Lord will bless my soul;
Wrestle on, Jacob,
O he would not let him go!

Fisherman Peter, out at sea,
He cast his net all in the sea;
He catch no fish, but he catch some soul,
And he would not let him go!

title: Poor Rosy
origin: Slave Songs of the United States (1867), No. 9, page 7; one of the songs Lucy McKim Garrison first transcribed in the Sea Islands.
note: Source: Slave Songs of the United States (1867), No. 9. Independent PD confirmation: Yale's Gullah Geechee Spirituals Project, which reproduces the 1867 text.
verses:
Poor Rosy, poor gal,
Poor Rosy, poor gal,
Rosy break my poor heart,
Heaven shall be my home.

I cannot stay in hell one day,
Heaven shall be my home;
I'll sing and pray my soul away,
Heaven shall be my home.

Got hard trial in my way,
Heaven shall be my home;
When I talk, I talk with God,
Heaven shall be my home.

title: Hold Your Light
origin: Slave Songs of the United States (1867), No. 12, page 10; a Sea Islands rowing/shout song.
note: Source: Slave Songs of the United States (1867), No. 12. Independent PD confirmation: Yale's Gullah Geechee Spirituals Project, which reproduces the 1867 text.
verses:
Hold your light, Brother Robert,
Hold your light,
Hold your light on Canaan's shore.

Hold your light, hold your light,
Hold your light,
Hold your light on Canaan's shore.

title: No Man Can Hinder Me
origin: Slave Songs of the United States (1867), No. 14, pages 10-11; from the South Carolina Sea Islands.
note: Source: Slave Songs of the United States (1867), No. 14. Independent PD confirmation: the Negro Spirituals Database and PD Info, both documenting the 1867 collection origin.
verses:
Walk in, kind Saviour,
No man can hinder me!
Walk in, sweet Jesus,
No man can hinder me!

You better pray, the world's a-going,
No man can hinder me!
If you want to find your way to God,
The gospel highway must be trod,
No man can hinder me!

title: Lay This Body Down
origin: Slave Songs of the United States (1867), No. 26; from the Port Royal Islands. Famously praised by Col. T. W. Higginson for the line 'I know moonrise.'
note: Source: Slave Songs of the United States (1867), No. 26. Independent PD confirmation: T. W. Higginson's 1867 Atlantic Monthly essay 'Negro Spirituals' (public domain), which quotes the song, corroborated by PD Info.
verses:
I know moonrise, I know starrise,
Lay this body down;
I walk in the moonlight, I walk in the starlight,
To lay this body down.

I'll walk in the graveyard, I'll walk through the graveyard,
To lay this body down;
I'll lie in the grave and stretch out my arms,
Lay this body down.

title: Turn, Sinner, Turn O!
origin: Slave Songs of the United States (1867), No. 48, pages 36-37; from the South Carolina Sea Islands.
note: Source: Slave Songs of the United States (1867), No. 48. Independent PD confirmation: PD Info's public-domain music reference, which lists the 1867 collection as public domain.
verses:
Turn, sinner, turn today,
Turn, sinner, turn O!
Turn, sinner, turn today,
Turn, sinner, turn O!

title: The Good Old Way
origin: Slave Songs of the United States (1867), No. 104; contributed by George H. Allan of Nashville, Tennessee. The earliest known form of the song now widely called 'Down in the River to Pray.'
note: Source: Slave Songs of the United States (1867), No. 104. Independent PD confirmation: Wikipedia, 'Down in the River to Pray,' which names this 1867 entry as the earliest published version.
verses:
As I went down in the valley to pray,
Studying about that good old way,
When you shall wear the starry crown,
Good Lord, show me the way.

O mourner, let's go down,
Let's go down, let's go down;
O mourner, let's go down,
Down in the valley to pray.

O sinner, let's go down,
Let's go down, let's go down;
O sinner, let's go down,
Down in the valley to pray.

title: My Father, How Long?
origin: Slave Songs of the United States (1867); a freedom spiritual the editors note was suppressed before the war and openly sung after emancipation.
note: Source: Slave Songs of the United States (1867), 'My Father, How Long?' Independent PD confirmation: PD Info's public-domain music reference, which lists the 1867 collection as public domain.
verses:
My father, how long,
My father, how long,
My father, how long,
Poor sinner suffer here?

And it won't be long,
And it won't be long,
And it won't be long,
Poor sinner suffer here.

We'll soon be free,
We'll soon be free,
We'll soon be free,
The Lord will call us home.

title: Lord, Remember Me
origin: Slave Songs of the United States (1867); a Sea Islands spiritual of petition.
note: Source: Slave Songs of the United States (1867), 'Lord, Remember Me.' Independent PD confirmation: PD Info's public-domain music reference, which lists the 1867 collection as public domain.
verses:
O Lord, remember me,
O Lord, remember me;
Remember me as the year roll round,
Lord, remember me.

When I'm a-going down the stream of time,
Lord, remember me;
I want-a Jesus for my friend,
Lord, remember me.
